title: The Three Decisions Every Independent Hotel Makes Alone
summary: Three decisions decide whether a hotel keeps a direct booking: the phone, the information, and the booking path. A chain makes them once. Most hotels make them alone.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### How many hotels in Germany are independent?


The split covers Germany, Austria, and Switzerland together. Of 26,707 hotels with a live website, 60.4% are confirmed single-operator independents, 22.0% are confirmed group-operated, and 17.6% are unresolved. The unresolved hotels stay in their own share. Germany accounts for 74% of the hotels in the scan. A Germany-only independent share is not what this scan measured.


At a confirmed independent, phone coverage, information maintenance, and the booking path are decided at that one property.


### What is the average hotel size in the DACH region?


This scan gives a distribution, not an average. Among hotels with a known room count, 66.3% have fewer than 50 rooms, which is small enough that one person makes the phone, information, and booking-path decisions. A public chain census counts a different stock.


The[Horwath HTL DACH Region Hotels & Chains Report 2025](https://horwathhtl.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/DACH-Hotel-Chains-Report_2025.pdf) , with figures as of 30 June 2025, puts chain penetration at 9.2% of hotels and 36.5% of keys. Chains are a small share of properties and a much larger share of rooms, because the chain hotel is bigger. That is a brand-and-room count across the full hotel stock, not the operator split in this article.


### Why don't hotels have standardized phone systems?


The phone-coverage decision sits at the property. Of the website-bearing hotels in the scan, 60.4% are confirmed single-operator independents, so the operator on site chooses who answers, including after the desk closes. A chain can set that rule once for every house. A group might have a central team and still leave coverage uneven.


What an unanswered phone costs is measured separately,[after hours](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/what-happens-when-a-guest-calls-your-hotel-after-hours) and[across the market](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/the-state-of-hotel-missed-calls) .


### Does hotel size affect technology adoption?


The size figure says who is in the building to make the three decisions. Among hotels with a known room count, 66.3% have fewer than 50 rooms, so the general manager, the front desk, and often the owner choose the phone coverage, the information, and the booking path. Room count and group membership are different facts.


The operator split is 60.4% confirmed independent, 22.0% confirmed group-operated, and 17.6% unresolved. The size figure describes that staff layer. It does not rank hotels by which systems they run.


### Who makes technology decisions at an independent hotel?


The operator of that property. The decisions are who answers the phone after the desk closes, whose job it is to keep the website, the phone, and the property management system accurate, and whether a guest can finish a booking on the hotel's own site. At a confirmed independent there is no group IT team and no central operations desk above the hotel.


The general manager is the head office.
